body:
# Independent audit: optimal geometric exit over the whole critical menu


`candidate bb78a1a25bcd2390`.
Result: **PASS after the boundary wording corrections listed below**.
The exact verifier `supporting computation verify_whole_critical_menu_exit_cost_simplex_chains.py`
was independently rerun and passed its strict-profile, cap-mass,
optimal-tilt, exit-cost, and above-target checks.

The full argument was checked against the archived exact-depth theorem,
the stopped-row definitions, and the attained critical-cap selection
theorem. The numerical verifier is not used as a substitute for the
all-direction classification.

## 1. All critical directions and all integer tilts

The exact-depth dependency applies to A=epsilon T under the strict
inequality a=epsilon^d<rho_d. Evaluating the defining directional
profile at a canonical simplex direction gives
rho_d<=((d-1)/(d+1))^d<1, so the assumptions ensure A is genuinely
contained in T and all three integer fibers are as stated. The
archived theorem gives the unique deepest point and raw depth Q.

A vertical halfspace through that point has mass at least 1+a>Q.
For every nonvertical direction, the coupled endpoint profile gives
the lower bound f(u)+min(a,q(u)). If q(u)<a, the STRICT profile gap
rho_d>a makes the cap mass strictly larger than Q. If q(u)>=a,
equality forces f(u)=gamma. The audited ordinary simplex equality
classification then restricts u to the d+1 canonical vertex directions.
This is the essential step ruling out other continuous orientations;
it would not follow from checking finitely many canonical cap masses.

After this direction classification, the real tilt L remains arbitrary.
If L<b-min_A lambda_i, its right T threshold is below 2b, so that
right cap alone has more than a volume. If L>=b-min_A lambda_i,
the left A is fully captured, and the right cap must have zero
d-volume. That happens exactly when L>=1-b. The converse follows
because 1-b>=b-min_A lambda_i for d>=2. This checks every real L,
including negative tilts, full caps, and both supporting thresholds.

Any critical cap merely containing the unique deepest point also has
its boundary through that point. Otherwise it contains it strictly,
and raising its threshold slightly retains the point while removing
a positive own-fiber strip, contradicting raw depth Q. Thus there
is no omitted containing cap relevant to the full critical menu.

## 2. Original source constraints and the retained KKT row

The finite P_i,Q_i cover has residual-root obstacle vector (0,c,c).
Nonnegative sampled convex heights satisfy h_0>=c and
h_-+h_+>=2h_0. Jensen on their dth powers, d>=2, gives a lower
objective bound 3c^d, and equality requires all three heights c.
Thus the optimizer and its uniqueness are justified exactly.

Writing s=d c^(d-1), the displayed multipliers give the endpoint
stationarity equations s-mu_(0,+/-)=0 and middle equation
s-lambda_0+mu_(0,-)+mu_(0,+)=0. Their slope balance is -s+s=0.
Obstacle and convexity complementary slackness are preserved. The
coupling row pi_(0,j)=s has source mass 3s, correct target masses,
and barycenter zero; its normalized probabilities are all 1/3.

Every member of the classified menu has residual roots (0,c,1).
Adjoining it retains every old cap, every obstacle, and the exact KKT
data. Same-direction replacement also preserves all trace measures
and the actual source cover, as now justified separately in the source.
Arbitrary-direction replacement after deleting another canonical cap
is not used. The optimization therefore does not quietly discard
the source constraints in order to reduce its exit cost.

## 3. Actual intermediate sections and first exits

At z=-t a convex combination of the lifted generators has weights
lambda_-=t+lambda_+ and homothety scale

    1-(1-epsilon)lambda_-
      <=1-(1-epsilon)t.

The upper scale is attained using only the -1 and 0 fibers. Since
all homothetic copies about the origin are nested, this proves the
exact section formula, not merely one contained Minkowski section.
For z in [0,1], the two copies of T already generate the whole T
section, and all other generators lie in T.

For i>=1 the barycentric minimum on every negative-base section is
zero. For i=0 it is 1-[1-(1-epsilon)t]=(1-epsilon)t.
These different minima give exactly the two exit formulas; treating
lambda_0 as a linear coordinate vanishing at the origin would give
the wrong answer. All the exit fractions are strictly below one
under L>=1-b and d>=2. At their first exit the strict residual is
empty but the CLOSED residual is a nonempty supporting face of
zero d-volume. This is precisely the boundary object required in
the geometric stopped-row construction.

The rightward path retains positive residual throughout and the
self destination also has exit fraction one. Hence the correction
is exactly (s_-+2)/3. Minimizing the two explicit formulas over all
L>=1-b and every classified direction gives the attained value
(d+2)/3. The origin-vertex direction has the strictly larger
additional term (d+1)(1-epsilon)/3. No remaining angular optimization
is being assumed.

The best CLOSED residual projection is [-1/d,1]. The strict,
positive-residual projection is (-1/d,1]. The source now explicitly
distinguishes them. All other critical projections are nested inside
this one, so the scalar and projection optima are both attained here.

## 4. Corrections made during this audit

At minimal tilt L=1-b, the right T trace is its canonical vertex;
it is not empty as a set. The author replaced the earlier wording
by zero d-volume and explicitly retained that vertex. Likewise
same-direction replacement preserves trace MEASURES, not identical
sets: the old large-tilt right trace is empty whereas the new one
can be a singleton. Actual cover preservation is now justified by
the full left fiber, the unchanged middle canonical cover, and the
retained right Q_i cover. The closed/strict projection distinction
above was also added. These corrections do not change any constant.

## 5. Exact limitation of the obstruction

The lower bound (d+2)/3 genuinely obstructs an unconditional bound
one or a dimension-free bound on this GEOMETRIC reciprocal exit
correction, even after optimizing over the full critical menu while
retaining the KKT data. The gap from OC is exactly positive and
tends to zero as a decreases, so mere above-target near-equality
does not force that geometric correction to approach one.

For any fixed d>=2, the hitting weight is 1/3 and the minimum
EXCESS correction is (d-1)/3, both bounded away from zero as a->0.
Thus neither quantity can be bounded by a fixed finite multiple
of the fully captured destination volume a alone. The same is true
of that excess multiplied by the fixed positive source root c.

This does NOT obstruct every possible volume charge, nor does it
show that the actual unstopped residual-root inequality needs any
correction. Indeed the original normalized row has values (0,c,1),
and its exact expected residual root is

    (c+1)/3 < c,

because c=(1-gamma)^(1/d)>1/2 for d>=2. Thus the unmodified row
already satisfies its desired Jensen comparison with factor one.
The geometric shortening and barycenter repair overestimate the
needed comparison in this very example. A charge using other source
mass, cap geometry, several destinations, or a strictly below-target
premise is not refuted. This distinction is essential when using
the certificate to rule out a particular proof mechanism.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
